{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-al-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"0793f57dbf1e1709cf2e687a8aecc4a3553d411978c61c4437eb65295e66a225","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-al-class-d:lineage:79","source_registry_sha256":"ea8231e949706ecda9f2a398d6eaf9ab30e224ac7defb0e6291b764b84ed0d95","source_liveness_sha256":"e524456f547beacfeca0647b02ef401523e58aa5b835501e7cbdd821b6546315"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver condition, phones, fatigue and alcohol (DUI law and confusables)","heading":"C2 — Alcohol limits, DUI penalties, implied consent and confusables","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Alcohol limits, DUI penalties, implied consent and confusables

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A35
The manual says one bottle of beer holds about as much alcohol as an average shot of whiskey or a glass of wine, with the same effect on the average driver. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A35
Alcohol is a depressant rather than a stimulant, bringing drowsiness, blurred vision and slower reflexes and weakening judgment and coordination. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A35
A driver can be impaired before reaching the point of legal intoxication. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A35
State law forbids driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs, or of a drug or an alcohol-drug combination that leaves you unable to drive safely. [A35]
Why it matters: sitting in control of the vehicle counts, not only driving it.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A35
For commercial vehicle operators the unlawful blood alcohol level is .04% or more. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A35
For persons under 21 years of age the unlawful blood alcohol level is .02% or more. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A35
For school bus and daycare drivers the unlawful blood alcohol level is also .02% or more. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A35
For a first DUI conviction the penalty is a $600 to $2,100 fine, a jail term of up to one year, or both, and the license is suspended for 90 days. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A35
A second conviction within 10 years brings a $1,100 to $5,100 fine, up to one year in jail or both, a mandatory 48 hours in jail or 20 days of community service, and a one-year license revocation. [A35]
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A36
A third conviction brings a $2,100 to $10,100 fine, a three-year license revocation, and up to one year in jail with a mandatory minimum of 60 days that cannot be probated or suspended. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A36
A fourth or later conviction is a Class C felony with fines of $4,100 to $10,100, a five-year revocation, and imprisonment of at least one year and one day and no more than 10 years. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A36
Under the implied consent law, anyone driving on Alabama's public highways is treated as having agreed to chemical testing of blood, breath or urine for alcohol content. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A36
A driver arrested for DUI who refuses an officer's direction to take a chemical breath test will have the driver license suspended. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A36
People who feel stimulated after drinking are really experiencing lowered inhibitions, which strip away caution and self-control. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A36
Beer, wine or whiskey makes no difference; what counts is how much alcohol reaches the blood. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A36
Alcohol can hit you differently from one time to the next, and a small amount affects you more on an empty stomach than after eating. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F45 | anchor: A36
Black coffee, food or a cold shower may wake you but will not sober you, because the liver must break alcohol down over time before the body eliminates it. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-F46 | anchor: A36
The manual's reasons not to drink and drive are that alcohol dulls judgment, slows reflexes, impairs vision, harms coordination, removes inhibitions, breeds overconfidence and prevents concentration. [A36]
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A35
The general limit is .08 percent, but commercial operators are held to .04% and drivers under 21 and school bus or daycare drivers to .02%. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint blood-alcohol-limits; prereq_hint sec06-F27; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F33, sec06-F34, sec06-F35.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A35
Research puts the start of impairment for most drivers at.05 percent, below the.08 percent level that makes driving unlawful [A35] [A34].
Why it matters: group_hint blood-alcohol-limits; prereq_hint sec06-F24; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec06-F25.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A35
A first DUI conviction brings a 90-day suspension, while a second conviction within 10 years brings a one-year revocation. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint dui-penalties; prereq_hint sec06-F32; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F36, sec06-F37.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A36
A third conviction costs the license for three years, while a fourth or later conviction is a felony with a five-year revocation. [A36]
Why it matters: group_hint dui-penalties; prereq_hint sec06-F37; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec06-F38, sec06-F39.
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A34
The texting fines climb from $25 to $50 to $75, but the record penalty stays the same two points for every offense. [A34]
Why it matters: group_hint texting-law; prereq_hint sec06-F14; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec06-F15, sec06-F16.
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A34
A tired driver may get by with coffee and stretching, but a truly sleepy driver must leave the highway and nap, and drugs to stay awake are never the answer. [A34]
Why it matters: group_hint fatigue; prereq_hint sec06-F17; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec06-F18, sec06-F19.
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-al-d:alabama-law-enforcement-agency-alea-driv:handbook:pdf-0034]
